{{short description|Sufficient condition for a Hamiltonian cycle in a graph, based on its vertex's degrees}}
{{distinguish|text=the [[Erdős–Pósa theorem]]}}
'''Pósa's theorem''', in [[graph theory]], is a [[sufficient condition]] for the existence of a [[Hamiltonian path|Hamiltonian cycle]] based on the [[degree (graph theory)|degrees]] of the [[vertex (graph theory)|vertices]] in an undirected graph. It implies two other degree-based sufficient conditions, [[Dirac's theorem on Hamiltonian cycles]] and [[Ore's theorem]]. Unlike those conditions, it can be applied to graphs with a small number of low-degree vertices. It is named after [[Lajos Pósa (mathematician)|Lajos Pósa]], a protégé of [[Paul Erdős]] born in 1947, who discovered this theorem in 1962.

The Pósa condition for a finite undirected graph <math>G</math> having <math>n</math> vertices requires that, if the degrees of the <math>n</math> vertices in increasing order as
:<math>d_{1} \leq d_{2} \leq ... \leq d_{n},</math>
then for each index <math>k < n/2</math> the inequality <math>k < d_{k}</math> is satisfied.

Pósa's theorem states that if a finite undirected graph satisfies the Pósa condition, then that graph has a Hamiltonian cycle in it.
